halt_reason: Step 4(ii) could not be run, and nothing else is outstanding. Every other step is complete and green: step 0's five proofs of B02's guards all came out as the spec predicted (O-19 closed, earlier-tests seen red on GitHub), all 39 decision-table rows pass, and tests, lint and guards are clean (271 passed, ruff clean, 7 guards ok, no findings). What is missing is the lock's proof against GitHub itself: 20 racing acquire pairs and 20 racing take_over pairs on lock/zz-proof-* references. This session's egress proxy denies every GitHub reference write - POST, PATCH and DELETE on /git/refs all return 403 'Write access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy' - and a git-protocol reference delete is refused too, so there is no route to it from here and the proxy's own guidance says not to look for one. The two API claims the lock design rests on therefore remain [Likely] rather than [Certain - run]: GitHub's docs, read fresh on 19 Nov, confirm that force defaults to false and means 'make sure the update is a fast-forward update', but state the status code for neither a duplicate create nor a refused non-fast-forward. Step 4(i)'s 40 races against a local bare repository pass and prove the lock protocol yields exactly one winner GIVEN a backend with those two properties; that backend is a test-side emulation and is not evidence that GitHub has them. The founder cleared this shape of finish at about 20:01 UTC on 19 Nov: build everything else and halt on 4(ii) alone.
halt_options: 1. The founder runs step 4(ii) by hand from a session with reference-write access (the desktop app on his Mac, with his own gh auth): 20 racing acquire pairs and 20 racing take_over pairs on references named lock/zz-proof-*, confirm exactly one winner in each of the 40 pairs, delete the references, and paste the count and one sample pair of API responses into reports/B03.md. Nothing in this build changes. 2. Hand step 4(ii) to B05, which is the build that attacks GitHub's rules from the automation's own account and is already set up to read API refusals back and paste them; B04 does not depend on the proof, only on the code. 3. If either race shows two winners, or GitHub accepts a non-fast-forward update with force: false, the spec's second Halt-if fires: the lock design is wrong, and the alternative to propose is a lock held as an issue assigned through the API. Also outstanding, and not a halt: two git references this session created and cannot delete - claude/b04 (reset to v2-build's commit, so it carries no proof content) and lock/zz-proof-probe. The first matters because facts.py reads build branches.
